summary.text: Paul Mark is a Democratic state senator from Massachusetts who has represented the Berkshire, Hampden, Franklin, and Hampshire District since January 2023 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
An attorney, he served in the Massachusetts House of Representatives from 2011 to 2023.

paragraphs.text: Mark earned a bachelor's degree in economics and finance from Southern New Hampshire University in 2005, a master's degree in labor from the University of Massachusetts Amherst in 2007, a juris doctor from Suffolk University in 2009, an associate degree in telecommunications from Springfield Technical Community College in 2010, and a doctorate in law and public policy from Northeastern University in 2010.

His career experience includes working as an attorney with the Law Offices of Paul W. Mark, as a visiting professor at the Massachusetts College of Liberal Arts, and as an adjunct professor at Greenfield Community College.
Mark represented the 2nd Berkshire District in the Massachusetts House of Representatives from 2011 to 2023, when Tricia Farley-Bouvier succeeded him.
He assumed office in the Senate on January 4, 2023.

For the 2025-2026 session he chairs the Joint Committee on Tourism, Arts and Cultural Development, is vice chair of the Joint Committees on Bonding, Capital Expenditures, and State Assets and on Transportation, and sits on the Senate Ways and Means Committee.
